standard.title: Counter Weighing Machines — Specification (First Revision) (काउंटर वजन मशीनें — विशिष्टि (पहला पुनरीक्षण))
standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes the quality, material, design, construction, accuracy classes, performance limits, and testing specifications for counter weighing machines (historically referred to as counter machines) of capacities up to and including 50 kg. These are equal-arm weighing balances with pans supported above the beam, used extensively in commercial trade transactions to ensure legal metrology compliance, measurement accuracy, and consumer protection.

version.current_version: First Revision, March 2026 (superseding the classic first edition, IS 1434 : 1959)

certification.description: Mandatory model approval and verification sealing under State Legal Metrology Acts and Rules. Manufacturers must possess a valid model approval license, and each individual machine must be physically verified, tested, and lead-stamped by a State Legal Metrology Inspector to be legally used or sold for trade in India.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, dimensional parameters, wall thicknesses, and capacities must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
A counter machine is defined as an equal-arm weighing instrument, of capacity not exceeding 50 kg, the pans of which are supported above the beam on vertical stays to maintain lateral stability.

Knife-edges and bearings must be manufactured from high-carbon steel, alloy steel, or agate. Hardened steel knife-edges must have a minimum hardness of 60 HRC (700 HV) to prevent blunting under heavy wear.

When the goods pan is in the form of a scoop, the counter machine must remain within the prescribed limits of error if half the full capacity load is placed against the middle of the back of the scoop and the remaining half is placed at any other position on the scoop.

When the goods pan is not a scoop, the scale must indicate the same weight within half the prescribed limits of maximum permissible error when a load equal to half the capacity is placed on the goods pan and moved anywhere within a distance from the center equal to one-third of the length of the pan.

To prevent unauthorized adjustments, each counter machine must carry a conspicuous plug or stud of soft lead. The plug or stud must be undercut or recessed to be irremovable, allowing the State Legal Metrology Inspector to emboss the official year and authority seal.
